rules.rule_name: Initialize Add User Session on First Entry
rules.rule_description: When a user accesses the Add User screen for the first time in a session, the system initializes the form by clearing all input fields and positioning the cursor on the First Name field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1:Initialize Add User Session
Set empty fields, cursor to First Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid session exists (EIBCALEN is not zero) and the program has not been re-entered yet (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is FALSE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Add User screen is accessed for the first time within the current session
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the session as re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER set to TRUE), clears the screen output area (COUSR1AO set to LOW-VALUES), and positions the cursor on the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI set to -1)

rules.rule_name: Display Add User Screen with Header Information
rules.rule_description: Every time the Add User screen is displayed, the system populates the screen header with current application titles, program name, transaction ID, current date, and current time before rendering the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2:Display Add User Screen
Populate header with title, program,
transaction, date, time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add User screen is ready to be sent to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to display the Add User screen (COUSR1A in mapset COUSR01)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with: Application Title 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) into TITLE01O, Application Title 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) into TITLE02O, current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into TRNNAMEO, current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) into PGMNAMEO, current date formatted as MM/DD/YY into CURDATEO, and current time formatted as HH:MM:SS into CURTIMEO; then sends the screen with ERASE and CURSOR options

rules.rule_name: Receive User Input from Add User Screen
rules.rule_description: When the user submits the Add User screen, the system captures all entered data including First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type from the screen map.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3:Receive User Input
Capture First Name, Last Name,
User ID, Password, User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid session exists and the program has been previously re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user interacts with the Add User screen and the system receives the screen input
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads all input fields from map COUSR1A (mapset COUSR01) into COUSR1AI, capturing First Name (FNAMEI), Last Name (LNAMEI), User ID (USERIDI), Password (PASSWDI), and User Type (USRTYPEI)

rules.rule_name: Handle PF3 Key - Navigate Back to Admin Menu
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 on the Add User screen, the system navigates back to the Admin Menu screen without saving any entered data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4:Handle PF3 Key
Navigate back to Admin Menu COADM01C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen with or without data entered in the fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key (EIBAID = DFHPF3)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to Admin Menu (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM = 'COADM01C'), records the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) in CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, records the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) in CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, resets program context (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = ZEROS), and transfers control to COADM01C passing the communication area

rules.rule_name: Handle PF4 Key - Clear All Fields and Redisplay Blank Form
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF4 on the Add User screen, the system clears all input fields and any messages, then redisplays a blank Add User form.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5:Handle PF4 Key
Clear all fields and redisplay blank form

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen with data entered in one or more fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF4 key (EIBAID = DFHPF4)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears all input fields by setting to SPACES: User ID (USERIDI of COUSR1AI), First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI), Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI), Password (PASSWDI of COUSR1AI), User Type (USRTYPEI of COUSR1AI), and the message area (WS-MESSAGE); positions the cursor on First Name (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI = -1); then redisplays the blank Add User screen

rules.rule_name: Handle Invalid Key Press on Add User Screen
rules.rule_description: When the user presses any key other than ENTER, PF3, or PF4 on the Add User screen, the system displays an invalid key error message and returns focus to the First Name field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6:Handle Invalid Key Press
Display invalid key error message
Focus on First Name field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key other than ENTER (DFHENTER), PF3 (DFHPF3), or PF4 (DFHPF4)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), positions the cursor on the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI = -1), displays the invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) in the message area (WS-MESSAGE), and redisplays the Add User screen with the error message

rules.rule_name: Validate First Name is Not Empty
rules.rule_description: When the user submits the Add User form, the system validates that the First Name field has been provided. If empty, an error is displayed and no further validation is performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7:Validate First Name
Error: First Name can NOT be empty
Focus on First Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The First Name field (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'First Name can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI = -1), redisplays the Add User screen with the error message, and stops further field validation

rules.rule_name: Validate Last Name is Not Empty
rules.rule_description: When the First Name is valid, the system validates that the Last Name field has been provided. If empty, an error is displayed and no further validation is performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8:Validate Last Name
Error: Last Name can NOT be empty
Focus on Last Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen and First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The Last Name field (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the Last Name field (LNAMEL of COUSR1AI = -1), redisplays the Add User screen with the error message, and stops further field validation

rules.rule_name: Validate User ID is Not Empty
rules.rule_description: When First Name and Last Name are valid, the system validates that the User ID field has been provided. If empty, an error is displayed and no further validation is performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9:Validate User ID
Error: User ID can NOT be empty
Focus on User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen, First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, and Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID field (USERIDI of COUSR1AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'User ID can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the User ID field (USERIDL of COUSR1AI = -1), redisplays the Add User screen with the error message, and stops further field validation

rules.rule_name: Validate Password is Not Empty
rules.rule_description: When First Name, Last Name, and User ID are valid, the system validates that the Password field has been provided. If empty, an error is displayed and no further validation is performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10:Validate Password
Error: Password can NOT be empty
Focus on Password

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen, First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, and User ID (USERIDI of COUSR1AI) is not empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The Password field (PASSWDI of COUSR1AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'Password can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the Password field (PASSWDL of COUSR1AI = -1), redisplays the Add User screen with the error message, and stops further field validation

rules.rule_name: Validate User Type is Not Empty
rules.rule_description: When First Name, Last Name, User ID, and Password are all valid, the system validates that the User Type field has been provided. If empty, an error is displayed and no further validation is performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11:Validate User Type
Error: User Type can NOT be empty
Focus on User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen, First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, User ID (USERIDI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, and Password (PASSWDI of COUSR1AI) is not empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The User Type field (USRTYPEI of COUSR1AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'User Type can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the User Type field (USRTYPEL of COUSR1AI = -1), redisplays the Add User screen with the error message, and stops further field validation

rules.rule_name: Prepare New User Record for Saving
rules.rule_description: When all five mandatory fields pass validation, the system maps the screen input values into the user security record structure in preparation for saving to the security file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12:Prepare New User Record
Map User ID, First Name, Last Name,
Password, User Type to record structure

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen and all five fields — First Name (FNAMEI), Last Name (LNAMEI), User ID (USERIDI), Password (PASSWDI), and User Type (USRTYPEI) — are non-empty (no error flag set, ERR-FLG-ON is FALSE)
acceptance_criteria.When: All field validations pass successfully
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system maps the screen values to the security user record: User ID (USERIDI of COUSR1AI) to SEC-USR-ID, First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) to SEC-USR-FNAME, Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI) to SEC-USR-LNAME, Password (PASSWDI of COUSR1AI) to SEC-USR-PWD, and User Type (USRTYPEI of COUSR1AI) to SEC-USR-TYPE

rules.rule_name: Save New User Record to Security File
rules.rule_description: After preparing the new user record, the system writes it to the User Security File using the User ID as the unique record key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13:Save New User to Security File
Write record using User ID as key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The new user record has been prepared with User ID (SEC-USR-ID), First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME), Password (SEC-USR-PWD), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to write the new user record to the User Security File (WS-USRSEC-FILE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system writes the complete user record (SEC-USER-DATA) to the User Security File using SEC-USR-ID as the unique record key, and captures the write response for outcome evaluation

rules.rule_name: Confirm Successful User Addition
rules.rule_description: When a new user is successfully saved to the security file, the system clears all input fields and displays a green confirmation message identifying the newly added user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14:Confirm Successful User Addition
Clear fields, display green success message
User added successfully

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write a new user record to the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.When: The write operation completes successfully (DFHRESP NORMAL)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears all input fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type set to SPACES, WS-MESSAGE set to SPACES, cursor positioned to First Name with FNAMEL = -1), sets the message color to green (ERRMSGC of COUSR1AO = DFHGREEN), constructs and displays the success message 'User [SEC-USR-ID] has been added ...' in WS-MESSAGE, and redisplays the Add User screen

rules.rule_name: Handle Duplicate User ID on Save
rules.rule_description: When the system attempts to save a new user but the User ID already exists in the security file, the system rejects the addition and prompts the user to provide a different User ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15:Handle Duplicate User ID
Error: User ID already exist
Focus on User ID field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write a new user record to the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.When: The write operation fails because the User ID already exists in the file (DFHRESP DUPKEY or DFHRESP DUPREC)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'User ID already exist...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the User ID field (USERIDL of COUSR1AI = -1), and redisplays the Add User screen with the error message

rules.rule_name: Handle Unexpected User Save Failure
rules.rule_description: When the system encounters an unexpected error while saving the new user record (not a duplicate), it notifies the user that the addition failed and returns focus to the First Name field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
16:Handle User Save Failure
Error: Unable to Add User
Focus on First Name field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write a new user record to the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.When: The write operation fails for any reason other than a duplicate User ID (response is not DFHRESP NORMAL, DFHRESP DUPKEY, or DFHRESP DUPREC)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'Unable to Add User...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI = -1), and redisplays the Add User screen with the error message

rules.rule_name: Return to Sign-On Screen When No Session Exists
rules.rule_description: When the Add User program is invoked without an existing session context, the system redirects the user to the Sign-On screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
17:Return to Sign-On Screen
Navigate to COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add User program (COUSR1C) is invoked
acceptance_criteria.When: There is no prior session context (EIBCALEN = 0)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to Sign-On screen (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM = 'COSGN00C'), records the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) in CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, records the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) in CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, resets program context (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = ZEROS), and transfers control to COSGN00C passing the communication area

rules.rule_name: Maintain Session Context on Return
rules.rule_description: After every screen interaction, the system returns control to CICS while preserving the session communication area and transaction ID so the program can be re-invoked with full context on the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
18:Maintain Session Context
Return control with session communication area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed processing any user interaction on the Add User screen (display, validation error, or successful save)
acceptance_criteria.When: The current processing cycle completes and control is returned to CICS
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system returns to CICS specifying the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) and passing the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), ensuring all session state is preserved for the next user interaction

rules.rule_name: Redirect to Sign-On Screen When No Prior Session Exists
rules.rule_description: When the Add User program is entered without an existing session context, the system must redirect the user to the Sign-On screen to establish a valid session before proceeding.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redirect to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Add User screen and no prior session context exists (communication area length is zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects the absence of a prior session
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and transfers control to that screen, ending the current program flow

rules.rule_name: Determine Whether This Is the First Visit to the Add User Screen
rules.rule_description: When a valid session exists, the system must determine whether the user is visiting the Add User screen for the first time or returning after a prior interaction, in order to decide whether to initialize the screen or process submitted input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is This the First Visit?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid session context exists and the communication area has been loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the session re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the re-entry flag is NOT set (first visit), the system proceeds to initialize and display a blank Add User screen; if the re-entry flag IS set (returning visit), the system proceeds to receive and process the user's screen input

rules.rule_name: Mark the Add User Session as Active on First Visit
rules.rule_description: On the first visit to the Add User screen, the system must mark the session as active so that subsequent interactions are recognized as returning visits and the screen input is processed rather than re-initialized.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Session as Active

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid session exists and the Add User screen is being visited for the first time (re-entry flag is not set)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initializes the Add User screen for first-time display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The session re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to TRUE, ensuring that the next interaction with this screen is treated as a returning visit

rules.rule_name: Clear All Add User Screen Fields on First Visit
rules.rule_description: When the Add User screen is displayed for the first time, all output screen fields must be cleared to ensure the user is presented with a blank, clean form with no residual data from prior interactions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear All Screen Fields

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add User screen is being displayed for the first time within the current session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the Add User screen for initial display
acceptance_criteria.Then: All fields on the Add User output screen (COUSR1AO) are set to LOW-VALUES, clearing any previously held data including First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, User Type, and any message areas

rules.rule_name: Set Cursor Focus to First Name Field on Initial Screen Display
rules.rule_description: When the Add User screen is displayed for the first time, the cursor must be automatically positioned on the First Name input field to guide the user to begin data entry at the correct starting field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Cursor Focus to First Name Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add User screen is being prepared for its first-time display after all fields have been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up the screen for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor position is set to the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI is set to -1), so that when the screen is rendered, the cursor automatically appears in the First Name input field

rules.rule_name: Display the Add User Screen with Header Information
rules.rule_description: After initializing all fields and setting cursor focus, the system must display the Add User screen to the user, populated with current header information including application titles, transaction ID, program name, current date, and current time.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Add User Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add User screen fields have been cleared, the cursor has been set to the First Name field, and the session has been marked as active
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen to the user's terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen (COUSR1A from mapset COUSR01) is displayed with: (1) application title lines populated from system constants, (2) the current Transaction ID, (3) the current Program Name, (4) the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, (5) the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS, (6) all input fields blank, (7) no error messages, and (8) the cursor positioned on the First Name field

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the Add User screen, the system retrieves the current system date and time to be formatted and shown in the screen header.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Current System Date and Time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to display the Add User data entry screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header population process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time and stores it in the working date/time data area (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent formatting and display

rules.rule_name: Populate Application Title on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The Add User screen header must display the standard application title lines (Title Line 1 and Title Line 2) sourced from the central application configuration data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Application Title on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is populating the Add User screen header
acceptance_criteria.When: The application title fields are being set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the standard application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) into the screen header Title 1 field (TITLE01O) and the standard application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) into the screen header Title 2 field (TITLE02O)

rules.rule_name: Populate Program Name on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The Add User screen header must display the name of the currently executing program so users and support staff can identify the active program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Program Name on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is populating the Add User screen header
acceptance_criteria.When: The program name field is being set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) into the screen header Program Name field (PGMNAMEO)

rules.rule_name: Populate Transaction ID on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The Add User screen header must display the current transaction identifier so users can reference the active transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Transaction ID on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is populating the Add User screen header
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction ID field is being set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into the screen header Transaction Name field (TRNNAMEO)

rules.rule_name: Format and Populate Current Date in MM/DD/YY Format on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The current date must be formatted as MM/DD/YY before being displayed in the Add User screen header, extracting month, day, and two-digit year components from the system date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format and Populate Current Date MM/DD/YY on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system date has been retrieved and stored in the working date area (WS-CURDATE-DATA)
acceptance_criteria.When: The current date is being formatted for screen header display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system extracts the month component into WS-CURDATE-MM, the day component into WS-CURDATE-DD, and the last two digits of the year (positions 3-4) into WS-CURDATE-YY, then assembles the formatted MM/DD/YY date string (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) and places it into the screen header Current Date field (CURDATEO)

rules.rule_name: Format and Populate Current Time in HH:MM:SS Format on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The current time must be formatted as HH:MM:SS before being displayed in the Add User screen header, extracting hours, minutes, and seconds components from the system time.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format and Populate Current Time HH:MM:SS on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system date and time has been retrieved and stored in the working date/time area (WS-CURDATE-DATA)
acceptance_criteria.When: The current time is being formatted for screen header display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system extracts the hours component into WS-CURTIME-HH, the minutes component into WS-CURTIME-MM, and the seconds component into WS-CURTIME-SS, then assembles the formatted HH:MM:SS time string (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) and places it into the screen header Current Time field (CURTIMEO)

rules.rule_name: Display Pending Message in Screen Message Area
rules.rule_description: Any pending informational or error message that was set prior to displaying the Add User screen must be transferred to the visible screen message area so the user can see it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move Any Pending Message to Screen Message Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add User screen is about to be rendered and a message may be present in the working message area (WS-MESSAGE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen message area is being populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the content of the working message area (WS-MESSAGE) — which may contain a validation error message, a success confirmation, or spaces if no message is pending — into the screen's error/message display field (ERRMSGO)

rules.rule_name: Render Add User Data Entry Form to User
rules.rule_description: After all header and message fields have been populated, the fully assembled Add User data entry form must be sent to the user's terminal, clearing any previous screen content and positioning the cursor as directed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Render Add User Data Entry Form to User

acceptance_criteria.Given: All screen header fields, message area, and data entry fields have been populated in the output map (COUSR1AO)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen to the user's terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system renders the Add User form (map COUSR1A from mapset COUSR01) to the terminal, erasing any previously displayed content, and positions the cursor at the field designated by the cursor-positioning indicator, leaving the screen awaiting user input

flowchart TD

rules.rule_name: Capture User Input from Add User Screen
rules.rule_description: When a user submits the Add User screen, the system must capture all data entered across the five input fields — First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type — before proceeding to validate the submitted data or handle the key press action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture All Data Entered by User on Add User Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has previously been presented with the Add User screen and has entered data into one or more of the following fields: First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the Add User screen by pressing any key (Enter, PF3, PF4, or any other key)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures and retains all data entered by the user across all five fields — First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type — from the Add User screen into the input data area, making the submitted values available for subsequent key press handling and field-level validation

rules.rule_name: Fields Available for Processing After Screen Submission
rules.rule_description: The Add User screen collects exactly five user-provided data fields. All five fields must be captured upon screen submission so they are available for mandatory field validation and subsequent user record creation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Fields Captured:
- First Name
- Last Name
- User ID
- Password
- User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add User screen has been displayed to the user and the user has interacted with the screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures the following five fields from the screen submission: (1) First Name, (2) Last Name, (3) User ID, (4) Password, and (5) User Type — all of which are subsequently available for mandatory field validation and new user record creation

rules.rule_name: Screen Input Capture Precedes Key Press Handling
rules.rule_description: The system must complete the capture of all user-entered screen data before evaluating which key the user pressed and determining the appropriate action to take. Screen data capture is a mandatory prerequisite step to key press handling.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Key Press Handling

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is in an active session and has already been presented with the Add User screen at least once (the session is in re-entry state)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the Add User screen by pressing any key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system first completes capturing all user-entered field data from the screen, and only after successful capture does it proceed to evaluate the key pressed (Enter, PF3, PF4, or other) to determine the next action — ensuring no key press handling occurs before all submitted field values are available

key_functionalities.title: Handle PF3 Key
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses PF3 Key])
    B[Set Destination to\nAdmin Menu Screen\nCOADM01C]
    C{Destination\nProgram Set?}
    D[Default Destination to\nSign-On Screen\nCOSGN00C]
    E[Record Current Session Details\nTransaction ID and Program Name]

    B --> C

rules.rule_name: Set Admin Menu as Navigation Destination on PF3
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 on the User Add screen, the system designates the Admin Menu screen (COADM01C) as the target navigation destination before initiating the return navigation flow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Destination to Admin Menu Screen COADM01C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User Add screen with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Admin Menu screen (COADM01C) and initiates the return-to-previous-screen navigation process

rules.rule_name: Default Navigation Destination to Sign-On Screen When Destination is Missing
rules.rule_description: As a safety fallback during navigation, if the destination program has not been set or is blank, the system defaults the navigation target to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default Destination to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The navigation process has been initiated and the destination program field is either empty or contains no value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the destination program before navigating
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system overrides the missing destination and sets it to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) as the default navigation target

rules.rule_name: Capture Current Session Context Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before navigating away from the User Add screen, the system records the current session's Transaction ID and Program Name into the shared communication area, and resets the program context indicator to zero, so the destination screen has full knowledge of where the navigation originated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Session Details Transaction ID and Program Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined the navigation destination (either Admin Menu COADM01C or defaulted to Sign-On COSGN00C)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the destination screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current Transaction ID into the 'From Transaction ID' field of the communication area, records the current Program Name into the 'From Program' field of the communication area, and resets the Program Context indicator to zero

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Destination Screen with Session Context
rules.rule_description: The system transfers full control to the destination screen (Admin Menu COADM01C or Sign-On COSGN00C as fallback), passing along the complete session communication area so the destination screen has access to all relevant session information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Navigate to Admin Menu Screen with Current Session Context

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program has been set (Admin Menu COADM01C or defaulted to Sign-On COSGN00C) and the current session details (Transaction ID, Program Name, Program Context) have been recorded in the communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers full control to the destination screen and passes the complete session communication area (containing Transaction ID, Program Name, and Program Context) to the destination screen, so no further processing occurs on the User Add screen

rules.rule_name: Detect PF4 Key Press and Trigger Clear Screen Action
rules.rule_description: When the user presses the PF4 key on the Add User screen, the system recognizes this as a request to clear all entered data and restart data entry from a blank form.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: User Presses PF4 Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen and has pressed a function key
acceptance_criteria.When: The key pressed is PF4
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system initiates the Clear Current Screen process, which clears all input fields and redisplays a blank Add User form

rules.rule_name: Clear First Name Input Field
rules.rule_description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, the First Name input field on the Add User screen is reset to blank/empty.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear First Name Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The First Name input field (FNAMEI) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously entered value

rules.rule_name: Clear Last Name Input Field
rules.rule_description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, the Last Name input field on the Add User screen is reset to blank/empty.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Last Name Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Last Name input field (LNAMEI) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously entered value

rules.rule_name: Clear User ID Input Field
rules.rule_description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, the User ID input field on the Add User screen is reset to blank/empty.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear User ID Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID input field (USERIDI) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously entered value

rules.rule_name: Clear Password Input Field
rules.rule_description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, the Password input field on the Add User screen is reset to blank/empty.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Password Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Password input field (PASSWDI) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously entered value

rules.rule_name: Clear User Type Input Field
rules.rule_description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, the User Type input field on the Add User screen is reset to blank/empty.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear User Type Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User Type input field (USRTYPEI) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously entered value

rules.rule_name: Clear Existing Error or Status Message
rules.rule_description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, any existing error or status message currently displayed on the Add User screen is removed so the user sees a clean form without any prior messages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Any Existing Error or Status Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated, and there may be an existing error or status message displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message area (WS-MESSAGE and ERRMSGO) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously displayed error or status message from the screen

rules.rule_name: Set Cursor Focus to First Name Field After Clear
rules.rule_description: After clearing all fields during the PF4 operation, the system positions the cursor on the First Name field so the user can immediately begin fresh data entry without manually navigating to the first field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Cursor Focus to First Name Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 and all input fields and messages have been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the blank Add User form
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor is set to the First Name field (FNAMEL length indicator set to -1) so that focus is placed on First Name when the screen is rendered

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Header with Current Date, Time, and Program Information
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the blank Add User form after a PF4 clear, the system refreshes the screen header with the current date, current time, application titles, transaction ID, and program name to ensure the header information is always up to date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Blank Add User Form

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to display the blank Add User form following a PF4 clear operation
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header population routine is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID), the current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME), the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY), and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS)

rules.rule_name: Display Blank Add User Form with Cleared Fields and No Messages
rules.rule_description: After all fields are cleared and the header is populated, the system sends the blank Add User form to the user's screen, erasing any previous screen content and positioning the cursor on the First Name field, enabling the user to begin fresh data entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Blank Add User Form

acceptance_criteria.Given: All input fields have been cleared to spaces, the message area is empty, the cursor is set to the First Name field, and the screen header has been populated with current date, time, transaction ID, and program name
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen (Map COUSR1A from Mapset COUSR01) to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is fully erased and redrawn showing a blank Add User form with no data in any input field, no error or status message displayed, the cursor positioned on the First Name field, and the header showing current date, time, transaction ID, and program name — allowing the user to begin fresh data entry

key_functionalities.title: Handle Invalid Key Press
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses a Key])
    B{Is Key\nEnter, PF3,\nor PF4?}
    C[Set Error Indicator]
    D[Load Invalid Key\nError Message]
    E[Set Cursor Focus\nto First Name Field]
    F[Redisplay Add User Screen\nwith Error Message]
    G([User Views Error\nand Corrects Key Action])

    A --> B
    B -->|No - Any Other Key| C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G

rules.rule_name: Detect Invalid Key Press on Add User Screen
rules.rule_description: When a user presses any key other than Enter, PF3, or PF4 on the Add User screen, the system identifies it as an invalid key action and triggers the error handling flow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Key Enter, PF3, or PF4?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen and has previously entered or not entered any data in the user fields (First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, User Type)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key that is NOT the Enter key, NOT PF3, and NOT PF4
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies the key press as invalid and initiates the invalid key error handling process, without processing any entered data or performing any save operation

rules.rule_name: Set Error Indicator on Invalid Key Press
rules.rule_description: When an invalid key is detected, the system activates the error indicator flag to signal that an error condition exists, which will control subsequent screen display behavior.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Indicator

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed a key on the Add User screen that is not Enter, PF3, or PF4
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects the key press is invalid (falls into the 'any other key' category)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error indicator flag to 'Y' (active/on), marking the current interaction as an error state so the screen is redisplayed in error mode

rules.rule_name: Load Invalid Key Error Message
rules.rule_description: When an invalid key press is detected, the system loads the standard invalid key error message into the screen message area to inform the user of the incorrect action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Load Invalid Key Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error indicator has been set due to an invalid key press on the Add User screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the invalid key error condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system loads the standard application-defined invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE), which will be displayed to the user in the error message area of the Add User screen

rules.rule_name: Set Cursor Focus to First Name Field on Invalid Key
rules.rule_description: After an invalid key press, the system directs the cursor to the First Name input field so the user's attention is guided to the beginning of the form for correction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Cursor Focus to First Name Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has detected an invalid key press and loaded the invalid key error message
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Add User screen with the error
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the cursor position indicator for the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI) to -1, which instructs the screen to place the cursor on the First Name input field when the screen is rendered

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Add User Screen with Invalid Key Error Message
rules.rule_description: The system redisplays the Add User screen with the invalid key error message visible, the cursor on the First Name field, and all previously entered data preserved, so the user can review the error and take the correct action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redisplay Add User Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error indicator is set to active, the invalid key error message is loaded into WS-MESSAGE, and the cursor is directed to the First Name field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen back to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with current date (MM/DD/YY format), current time (HH:MM:SS format), transaction ID, and program name; moves the error message from WS-MESSAGE into the screen error message display field (ERRMSGO of COUSR1AO); and redisplays the full Add User screen (MAP COUSR1A, MAPSET COUSR01) with the cursor positioned on the First Name field and all previously entered field values retained on screen

key_functionalities.title: Validate First Name
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Enter Key Pressed]) 
    B{Is First Name\nBlank or Empty?}
    C[Set Error Flag to ON]
    D[Set Error Message:\n'First Name can NOT be empty...']
    E[Set Cursor Focus\nto First Name Field]
    F[Display Add User Screen\nwith Error Message]
    G([Proceed to\nValidate Last Name])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - First Name is Empty| C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    B -->|No - First Name has Value| G

rules.rule_name: First Name Mandatory Field Validation
rules.rule_description: When a user submits the Add User form by pressing the Enter key, the system must verify that the First Name field contains a value. If the First Name field is blank or empty, the submission is rejected and the user is prompted to provide a First Name.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is First Name Blank or Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add User screen is displayed and the user has pressed the Enter key to submit the form
acceptance_criteria.When: The First Name field contains only blank spaces or is completely empty (low-values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) activate the error flag to indicate a validation failure, (2) set the error message to 'First Name can NOT be empty...', (3) position the cursor focus on the First Name field, and (4) redisplay the Add User screen showing the error message — no further field validations are performed and the user record is NOT saved

rules.rule_name: Error Flag Activation on First Name Validation Failure
rules.rule_description: When the First Name field is found to be blank or empty upon form submission, the system activates an internal error flag to signal that a validation error has occurred, preventing the user record from being saved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Flag to ON

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key to submit the Add User form
acceptance_criteria.When: The First Name field is blank or empty (spaces or low-values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to ON ('Y'), which prevents any further processing such as saving the new user record to the system

rules.rule_name: First Name Empty Error Message Assignment
rules.rule_description: When the First Name field fails the mandatory field check, the system assigns a specific, user-friendly error message to inform the user exactly which field requires attention and what the issue is.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Message: 'First Name can NOT be empty...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error flag has been activated due to the First Name field being blank or empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Add User screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error message displayed on the screen must be exactly: 'First Name can NOT be empty...'

rules.rule_name: Cursor Positioning to First Name Field on Validation Error
rules.rule_description: When the First Name field fails validation, the system automatically positions the screen cursor on the First Name input field to guide the user directly to the field that requires correction, improving the user experience.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Cursor Focus to First Name Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The First Name field has been found to be blank or empty upon form submission
acceptance_criteria.When: The Add User screen is being prepared for redisplay with the error message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor focus must be set to the First Name input field so that the user can immediately begin correcting the value without manually navigating to the field

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Add User Screen with First Name Validation Error
rules.rule_description: After detecting that the First Name field is empty and setting the appropriate error message and cursor position, the system redisplays the Add User screen so the user can see the error and make the necessary correction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Add User Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The First Name field is blank or empty, the error flag is ON, the error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...' has been set, and the cursor is positioned on the First Name field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen back to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Add User screen (COUSR1A) is redisplayed with: (1) the error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...' visible on screen, (2) the cursor positioned on the First Name field, (3) all previously entered data for other fields retained on screen, and (4) the screen header updated with current date and time

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Last Name Validation When First Name is Valid
rules.rule_description: When the First Name field contains a valid non-empty value, the system proceeds to the next sequential validation step — checking the Last Name field — as part of the mandatory field validation sequence for the Add User form.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Validate Last Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key to submit the Add User form
acceptance_criteria.When: The First Name field contains a non-blank, non-empty value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does not raise any error for the First Name field and proceeds immediately to validate the Last Name field as the next step in the sequential validation process

key_functionalities.title: Validate Last Name
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Enter Last Name Validation])
    B{Is Last Name\nBlank or Empty?}
    C[Set Error Flag\nError Message:\n'Last Name can NOT be empty...'\nSet Cursor Focus to Last Name Field]
    D[Display Add User Screen\nwith Error Message]
    E([Proceed to\nUser ID Validation])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Last Name is Empty| C
    C --> D
    D --> END1([End - Await User Correction])
    B -->|No - Last Name has Value| E

rules.rule_name: Last Name Mandatory Field Validation
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Last Name field is not blank or empty when a user submits the Add User form. This rule ensures that every new user record must have a Last Name value before it can be saved to the system.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Last Name Blank or Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen and has pressed the ENTER key to submit the form, and the First Name field has already been validated successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The Last Name field is blank or contains no value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error indicator to active, (2) set the error message to 'Last Name can NOT be empty...', (3) set the cursor focus to the Last Name input field, and (4) redisplay the Add User screen with the error message visible, halting further validation until the user corrects the Last Name field

rules.rule_name: Last Name Valid – Proceed to User ID Validation
rules.rule_description: When the Last Name field contains a valid non-blank value, the system proceeds to the next sequential validation step, which is the User ID field check. No action or message is triggered for the Last Name field itself.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to User ID Validation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen and has pressed the ENTER key to submit the form, and the First Name field has already been validated successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The Last Name field contains a non-blank, non-empty value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does not set any error flag or error message for the Last Name field, and immediately proceeds to validate the User ID field

rules.rule_name: Display Add User Screen with Last Name Error Message
rules.rule_description: When the Last Name validation fails, the system refreshes and redisplays the Add User screen, showing the error message to the user. The screen header is also refreshed with the current date, time, transaction ID, and program name before display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Add User Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Last Name field has been found to be blank or empty during form submission validation, and the error flag has been set with the message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' and cursor positioned on the Last Name field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is instructed to send the Add User screen back to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) populate the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction ID, and program name, (2) place the error message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' in the screen error message area, and (3) redisplay the Add User screen with all previously entered field values retained and the cursor positioned on the Last Name field, awaiting user correction

key_functionalities.title: Validate User ID
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD

    B{Has First Name\nand Last Name\nalready passed\nvalidation?}
    C{Is User ID\nBlank or Empty?}

    F[Set Cursor Focus\nto User ID Field]

    A --> B

    B -->|Yes - Proceed to\nUser ID check| C

    D --> E

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Cursor Focus to User ID Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has detected a duplicate User ID condition and has set the error message to 'User ID already exist...'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Add User screen with the error information
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the cursor position indicator for the User ID field to -1, which directs the screen cursor to be placed on the User ID input field when the screen is redisplayed

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Add User Screen with Duplicate User ID Error
rules.rule_description: After setting the duplicate User ID error state, error message, and cursor position, the system must redisplay the Add User screen so the user can see the error message and correct the User ID. The screen redisplay includes refreshing the header information with current date and time.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redisplay Add User Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The session error flag is set to active, the error message is set to 'User ID already exist...', and the cursor focus is directed to the User ID field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system invokes the Send Add User Screen process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must populate the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY format), current time (HH:MM:SS format), transaction ID, and program name, then display the Add User screen with the error message 'User ID already exist...' visible and the cursor positioned on the User ID field, allowing the user to enter a different User ID

key_functionalities.title: Handle User Save Failure
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Save New User to Security File\nWrite Attempted])
    B{Save Result?}
    C[Set Error Flag to ON]
    D[Set Error Message:\n'Unable to Add User...']
    E[Set Cursor Focus\nto First Name Field]
    F[Display Add User Screen\nwith Error Message]
    G([User Reviews Error\nand Can Retry])

    A --> B
    B -->|Unexpected Error Occurred| C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G

rules.rule_name: Detect Unexpected User Save Failure
rules.rule_description: When the system attempts to save a new user record to the security file and the result is neither a successful write nor a duplicate key/record condition, the system identifies this as an unexpected save failure and triggers the error handling path.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Result? → Unexpected Error Occurred

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new user record has been submitted for saving to the User Security File with all mandatory fields (First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, User Type) populated and the User ID is not a duplicate
acceptance_criteria.When: The save operation to the User Security File completes with an outcome that is not a successful write and not a duplicate User ID or duplicate record condition — i.e., an unexpected system or data error occurs
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must identify the result as an unexpected save failure and proceed to activate the error handling sequence, which includes setting the error flag, displaying an error message, and returning the Add User screen to the user for retry

rules.rule_name: Activate Error State on Unexpected Save Failure
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs during the save of a new user record, the system must activate the error flag to indicate that the current transaction is in an error state, preventing any further processing of the user record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Flag to ON

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to save a new user record to the User Security File and the save result is an unexpected error (not success, not duplicate)
acceptance_criteria.When: The unexpected error condition is detected from the save operation result
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the Error Flag to ON (value 'Y' in WS-ERR-FLG) to mark the transaction as failed and block any downstream processing of the user record

rules.rule_name: Display 'Unable to Add User' Error Message on Unexpected Save Failure
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs while saving a new user record, the system must set a specific business error message to inform the user that the add operation could not be completed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Message: 'Unable to Add User...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to save a new user record to the User Security File and the save result is an unexpected error (not success, not duplicate)
acceptance_criteria.When: The error flag has been set to ON due to the unexpected save failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the screen error message to exactly 'Unable to Add User...' (stored in WS-MESSAGE) so that this message will be presented to the user on the Add User screen

rules.rule_name: Reposition Cursor to First Name Field After Save Failure
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs while saving a new user record, the system must direct the user's cursor focus back to the First Name field on the Add User screen, guiding the user to review and re-enter data from the beginning of the form.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Cursor Focus to First Name Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has encountered an unexpected error while saving a new user record to the User Security File and the error message 'Unable to Add User...' has been set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Add User screen following the unexpected save failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the cursor position to the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI set to -1) so that when the Add User screen is redisplayed, the cursor is automatically placed on the First Name input field for the user to begin reviewing their input

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Add User Screen with Save Failure Error Message
rules.rule_description: After an unexpected error occurs during the save of a new user record, the system must redisplay the Add User screen with the error message and updated header information, allowing the user to review the error and retry the operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Add User Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has set the error flag to ON, the error message to 'Unable to Add User...', and the cursor focus to the First Name field following an unexpected save failure
acceptance_criteria.When: The system invokes the Send Add User Screen function (SEND-USRADD-SCREEN), which populates the screen header with the current Transaction ID, Program Name, current Date (MM/DD/YY), and current Time (HH:MM:SS) before sending the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Add User screen (COUSR1A from mapset COUSR01) must be redisplayed to the user with: (1) the error message 'Unable to Add User...' shown in the message area, (2) the cursor positioned on the First Name field, (3) all previously entered field values retained on screen, and (4) the screen header showing current date, time, transaction ID, and program name — enabling the user to review the error and retry adding the user

key_functionalities.title: Return to Sign
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Return to Sign-On Screen Triggered])
    B{No Prior Session\nExists?}
    C[Set Destination to\nSign-On Screen COSGN00C]
    D{Destination Program\nBlank or Not Set?}
    E[Default Destination to\nSign-On Screen COSGN00C]
    F[Record Current Transaction\nand Program in Session]
    G[Clear Session Context]
    H([Navigate User to\nSign-On Screen COSGN00C])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - No Session| C
    C --> D
    B -->|No - Session Exists| D
    D -->|Yes - Blank or Empty| E
    E --> F
    D -->|No - Destination is Set| F
    F --> G
    G --> H

rules.rule_name: Redirect to Sign-On Screen When No Prior Session Exists
rules.rule_description: When the User Add screen is invoked without any prior session context, the system must immediately redirect the user to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to establish a valid session before proceeding.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No Prior Session Exists?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User Add screen is accessed and no prior session context exists (communication area length is zero, indicating no active session has been established)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects the absence of a prior session context at program entry
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and initiates navigation to that screen, preventing access to the User Add functionality without a valid session

rules.rule_name: Default Destination to Sign-On Screen When Destination Program Is Not Set
rules.rule_description: Before navigating away from the User Add screen, the system must verify that a destination program has been explicitly set. If the destination is blank or not set, the system defaults the navigation target to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Destination Program Blank or Not Set?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to navigate the user away from the User Add screen and the destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is either blank (spaces) or contains no value (low-values)
acceptance_criteria.When: The return-to-previous-screen process is triggered and the destination program is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system overrides the blank or unset destination and sets it to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) as the default navigation target, ensuring no navigation occurs to an undefined screen

rules.rule_name: Record Current Transaction and Program in Session Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before navigating the user to another screen, the system must record the current transaction identifier and the current program name into the session context. This preserves the originating transaction and program information so the destination screen knows where the navigation originated from.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Transaction and Program in Session

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined the destination program and is preparing to navigate the user away from the User Add screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The navigation process records session origin details prior to transferring control
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures and stores the current transaction identifier (WS-TRANID) as the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the session communication area

rules.rule_name: Clear Session Program Context Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Immediately before transferring control to the destination screen, the system must reset the session program context to zero. This ensures that the destination screen treats the incoming navigation as a fresh entry rather than a re-entry, preventing stale context from affecting the destination screen's behavior.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Session Context

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has recorded the originating transaction and program in the session and is about to transfer control to the destination screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The session context is cleared as the final step before navigation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the session program context indicator (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) to zero, signaling to the destination screen that this is a new entry and not a re-entry from a previous interaction

rules.rule_name: Navigate User to Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: After all session context has been recorded and cleared, the system transfers control to the resolved destination screen (Sign-On screen COSGN00C), passing the updated session communication area so the destination screen has full context of the navigation origin.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Navigate User to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program has been set (either explicitly to COSGN00C or defaulted to COSGN00C), the originating transaction and program have been recorded, and the session program context has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer to the destination program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) passing the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) containing the originating transaction identifier, originating program name, and cleared program context, so the Sign-On screen can process the incoming navigation correctly

key_functionalities.title: Maintain Session Context
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([All User Interactions Complete])
    B[Preserve Current Session Data\nRetain all session information\nin Communication Area]
    C[Return Control to\nCurrent Transaction\nUsing same Transaction ID]
    D([Session Ready for\nNext User Interaction])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D

rules.rule_name: Preserve Session Communication Area Before Returning Control
rules.rule_description: At the end of every user interaction cycle, the system must retain all current session information — including the Transaction ID, Program Name, and the full Communication Area — so that the session context is not lost between interactions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Preserve Current Session Data
Retain all session information
in Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user interaction has completed (any key press has been processed — ENTER, PF3, PF4, or any other key) and the system is about to return control back to the transaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to end the current processing cycle
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must retain the current CARDDEMO-COMMAREA (containing session data including CDEMO-FROM-TRANID set to WS-TRANID, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM set to WS-PGMNAME, CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT, and CDEMO-PGM-REENTER flag) and pass it forward with the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) so that the next interaction resumes with full session continuity

rules.rule_name: Return Control to Current Transaction with Session Data
rules.rule_description: After every user interaction is fully processed — whether it results in a screen display, a navigation action, or a data save — the system must explicitly return control to the same transaction using the preserved Communication Area, ensuring the session remains active and ready for the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Return Control to
Current Transaction
Using same Transaction ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: All processing for the current user interaction has been completed, including any screen sends, validations, data writes, or navigation decisions
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the final return step at the end of MAIN-PARA
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system returns control using the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) and passes the full CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, so that the transaction remains active, the session state is preserved, and the system is ready to receive the next user interaction without loss of context

rules.rule_name: Session Continuity Across Navigation to Previous Screen
rules.rule_description: When the user navigates away from the User Add screen (e.g., via PF3 to Admin Menu or when no session exists and redirected to Sign-On), the system must stamp the Communication Area with the originating Transaction ID and Program Name before transferring control, ensuring the destination screen knows where the user came from.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Preserve Current Session Data
Retain all session information
in Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has triggered a navigation action (PF3 pressed to go to Admin Menu COADM01C, or no active session detected redirecting to Sign-On COSGN00C)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN procedure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) verify the destination program is set — if CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM is empty or low-values, default it to COSGN00C; (2) set CDEMO-FROM-TRANID to WS-TRANID (current transaction); (3) set CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM to WS-PGMNAME (current program name); (4) set CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT to zeros; and (5) transfer control to the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) passing the updated CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, so the destination screen has full context of the originating session

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid session exists (EIBCALEN is not zero) and the program has not been re-entered yet (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is FALSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Add User screen is accessed for the first time within the current session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the session as re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER set to TRUE), clears the screen output area (COUSR1AO set to LOW-VALUES), and positions the cursor on the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI set to -1)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Add User Session on First Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user accesses the Add User screen for the first time in a session, the system initializes the form by clearing all input fields and positioning the cursor on the First Name field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add User screen is ready to be sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to display the Add User screen (COUSR1A in mapset COUSR01)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with: Application Title 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) into TITLE01O, Application Title 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) into TITLE02O, current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into TRNNAMEO, current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) into PGMNAMEO, current date formatted as MM/DD/YY into CURDATEO, and current time formatted as HH:MM:SS into CURTIMEO; then sends the screen with ERASE and CURSOR options

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Add User Screen with Header Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the Add User screen is displayed, the system populates the screen header with current application titles, program name, transaction ID, current date, and current time before rendering the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid session exists and the program has been previously re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user interacts with the Add User screen and the system receives the screen input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads all input fields from map COUSR1A (mapset COUSR01) into COUSR1AI, capturing First Name (FNAMEI), Last Name (LNAMEI), User ID (USERIDI), Password (PASSWDI), and User Type (USRTYPEI)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive User Input from Add User Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits the Add User screen, the system captures all entered data including First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type from the screen map.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen with or without data entered in the fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key (EIBAID = DFHPF3)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to Admin Menu (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM = 'COADM01C'), records the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) in CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, records the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) in CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, resets program context (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = ZEROS), and transfers control to COADM01C passing the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle PF3 Key - Navigate Back to Admin Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the Add User screen, the system navigates back to the Admin Menu screen without saving any entered data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen with data entered in one or more fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF4 key (EIBAID = DFHPF4)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears all input fields by setting to SPACES: User ID (USERIDI of COUSR1AI), First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI), Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI), Password (PASSWDI of COUSR1AI), User Type (USRTYPEI of COUSR1AI), and the message area (WS-MESSAGE); positions the cursor on First Name (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI = -1); then redisplays the blank Add User screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle PF4 Key - Clear All Fields and Redisplay Blank Form
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF4 on the Add User screen, the system clears all input fields and any messages, then redisplays a blank Add User form.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key other than ENTER (DFHENTER), PF3 (DFHPF3), or PF4 (DFHPF4)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), positions the cursor on the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI = -1), displays the invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) in the message area (WS-MESSAGE), and redisplays the Add User screen with the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Invalid Key Press on Add User Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses any key other than ENTER, PF3, or PF4 on the Add User screen, the system displays an invalid key error message and returns focus to the First Name field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The First Name field (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'First Name can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI = -1), redisplays the Add User screen with the error message, and stops further field validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate First Name is Not Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits the Add User form, the system validates that the First Name field has been provided. If empty, an error is displayed and no further validation is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen and First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Last Name field (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the Last Name field (LNAMEL of COUSR1AI = -1), redisplays the Add User screen with the error message, and stops further field validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Last Name is Not Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the First Name is valid, the system validates that the Last Name field has been provided. If empty, an error is displayed and no further validation is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen, First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, and Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field (USERIDI of COUSR1AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'User ID can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the User ID field (USERIDL of COUSR1AI = -1), redisplays the Add User screen with the error message, and stops further field validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User ID is Not Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When First Name and Last Name are valid, the system validates that the User ID field has been provided. If empty, an error is displayed and no further validation is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen, First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, and User ID (USERIDI of COUSR1AI) is not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Password field (PASSWDI of COUSR1AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'Password can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the Password field (PASSWDL of COUSR1AI = -1), redisplays the Add User screen with the error message, and stops further field validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Password is Not Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When First Name, Last Name, and User ID are valid, the system validates that the Password field has been provided. If empty, an error is displayed and no further validation is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen, First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, User ID (USERIDI of COUSR1AI) is not empty, and Password (PASSWDI of COUSR1AI) is not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Type field (USRTYPEI of COUSR1AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'User Type can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the User Type field (USRTYPEL of COUSR1AI = -1), redisplays the Add User screen with the error message, and stops further field validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User Type is Not Empty
