all_rules.Rule_Description: When First Name, Last Name, User ID, and Password are all valid, the system validates that the User Type field has been provided. If empty, an error is displayed and no further validation is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Add User screen and all five fields — First Name (FNAMEI), Last Name (LNAMEI), User ID (USERIDI), Password (PASSWDI), and User Type (USRTYPEI) — are non-empty (no error flag set, ERR-FLG-ON is FALSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All field validations pass successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system maps the screen values to the security user record: User ID (USERIDI of COUSR1AI) to SEC-USR-ID, First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR1AI) to SEC-USR-FNAME, Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR1AI) to SEC-USR-LNAME, Password (PASSWDI of COUSR1AI) to SEC-USR-PWD, and User Type (USRTYPEI of COUSR1AI) to SEC-USR-TYPE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare New User Record for Saving
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all five mandatory fields pass validation, the system maps the screen input values into the user security record structure in preparation for saving to the security file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The new user record has been prepared with User ID (SEC-USR-ID), First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME), Password (SEC-USR-PWD), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to write the new user record to the User Security File (WS-USRSEC-FILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system writes the complete user record (SEC-USER-DATA) to the User Security File using SEC-USR-ID as the unique record key, and captures the write response for outcome evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save New User Record to Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After preparing the new user record, the system writes it to the User Security File using the User ID as the unique record key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write a new user record to the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation completes successfully (DFHRESP NORMAL)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears all input fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type set to SPACES, WS-MESSAGE set to SPACES, cursor positioned to First Name with FNAMEL = -1), sets the message color to green (ERRMSGC of COUSR1AO = DFHGREEN), constructs and displays the success message 'User [SEC-USR-ID] has been added ...' in WS-MESSAGE, and redisplays the Add User screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful User Addition
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new user is successfully saved to the security file, the system clears all input fields and displays a green confirmation message identifying the newly added user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write a new user record to the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation fails because the User ID already exists in the file (DFHRESP DUPKEY or DFHRESP DUPREC)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'User ID already exist...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the User ID field (USERIDL of COUSR1AI = -1), and redisplays the Add User screen with the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Duplicate User ID on Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system attempts to save a new user but the User ID already exists in the security file, the system rejects the addition and prompts the user to provide a different User ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write a new user record to the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation fails for any reason other than a duplicate User ID (response is not DFHRESP NORMAL, DFHRESP DUPKEY, or DFHRESP DUPREC)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'Unable to Add User...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI = -1), and redisplays the Add User screen with the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Unexpected User Save Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system encounters an unexpected error while saving the new user record (not a duplicate), it notifies the user that the addition failed and returns focus to the First Name field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add User program (COUSR1C) is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: There is no prior session context (EIBCALEN = 0)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to Sign-On screen (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM = 'COSGN00C'), records the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) in CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, records the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) in CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, resets program context (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = ZEROS), and transfers control to COSGN00C passing the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Sign-On Screen When No Session Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Add User program is invoked without an existing session context, the system redirects the user to the Sign-On screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed processing any user interaction on the Add User screen (display, validation error, or successful save)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current processing cycle completes and control is returned to CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system returns to CICS specifying the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) and passing the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), ensuring all session state is preserved for the next user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Maintain Session Context on Return
all_rules.Rule_Description: After every screen interaction, the system returns control to CICS while preserving the session communication area and transaction ID so the program can be re-invoked with full context on the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Add User screen and no prior session context exists (communication area length is zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects the absence of a prior session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and transfers control to that screen, ending the current program flow

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redirect to Sign-On Screen When No Prior Session Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Add User program is entered without an existing session context, the system must redirect the user to the Sign-On screen to establish a valid session before proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid session context exists and the communication area has been loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the session re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the re-entry flag is NOT set (first visit), the system proceeds to initialize and display a blank Add User screen; if the re-entry flag IS set (returning visit), the system proceeds to receive and process the user's screen input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Whether This Is the First Visit to the Add User Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid session exists, the system must determine whether the user is visiting the Add User screen for the first time or returning after a prior interaction, in order to decide whether to initialize the screen or process submitted input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid session exists and the Add User screen is being visited for the first time (re-entry flag is not set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes the Add User screen for first-time display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The session re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to TRUE, ensuring that the next interaction with this screen is treated as a returning visit

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark the Add User Session as Active on First Visit
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the first visit to the Add User screen, the system must mark the session as active so that subsequent interactions are recognized as returning visits and the screen input is processed rather than re-initialized.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add User screen is being displayed for the first time within the current session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Add User screen for initial display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields on the Add User output screen (COUSR1AO) are set to LOW-VALUES, clearing any previously held data including First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, User Type, and any message areas

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Add User Screen Fields on First Visit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Add User screen is displayed for the first time, all output screen fields must be cleared to ensure the user is presented with a blank, clean form with no residual data from prior interactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add User screen is being prepared for its first-time display after all fields have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor position is set to the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI is set to -1), so that when the screen is rendered, the cursor automatically appears in the First Name input field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Cursor Focus to First Name Field on Initial Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Add User screen is displayed for the first time, the cursor must be automatically positioned on the First Name input field to guide the user to begin data entry at the correct starting field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add User screen fields have been cleared, the cursor has been set to the First Name field, and the session has been marked as active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen to the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen (COUSR1A from mapset COUSR01) is displayed with: (1) application title lines populated from system constants, (2) the current Transaction ID, (3) the current Program Name, (4) the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, (5) the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS, (6) all input fields blank, (7) no error messages, and (8) the cursor positioned on the First Name field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display the Add User Screen with Header Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: After initializing all fields and setting cursor focus, the system must display the Add User screen to the user, populated with current header information including application titles, transaction ID, program name, current date, and current time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to display the Add User data entry screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time and stores it in the working date/time data area (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent formatting and display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Add User screen, the system retrieves the current system date and time to be formatted and shown in the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating the Add User screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The application title fields are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the standard application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) into the screen header Title 1 field (TITLE01O) and the standard application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) into the screen header Title 2 field (TITLE02O)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Application Title on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Add User screen header must display the standard application title lines (Title Line 1 and Title Line 2) sourced from the central application configuration data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating the Add User screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program name field is being set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) into the screen header Program Name field (PGMNAMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Program Name on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Add User screen header must display the name of the currently executing program so users and support staff can identify the active program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating the Add User screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction ID field is being set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into the screen header Transaction Name field (TRNNAMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Transaction ID on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Add User screen header must display the current transaction identifier so users can reference the active transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system date has been retrieved and stored in the working date area (WS-CURDATE-DATA)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current date is being formatted for screen header display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the month component into WS-CURDATE-MM, the day component into WS-CURDATE-DD, and the last two digits of the year (positions 3-4) into WS-CURDATE-YY, then assembles the formatted MM/DD/YY date string (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) and places it into the screen header Current Date field (CURDATEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Populate Current Date in MM/DD/YY Format on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current date must be formatted as MM/DD/YY before being displayed in the Add User screen header, extracting month, day, and two-digit year components from the system date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system date and time has been retrieved and stored in the working date/time area (WS-CURDATE-DATA)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current time is being formatted for screen header display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the hours component into WS-CURTIME-HH, the minutes component into WS-CURTIME-MM, and the seconds component into WS-CURTIME-SS, then assembles the formatted HH:MM:SS time string (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) and places it into the screen header Current Time field (CURTIMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Populate Current Time in HH:MM:SS Format on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current time must be formatted as HH:MM:SS before being displayed in the Add User screen header, extracting hours, minutes, and seconds components from the system time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add User screen is about to be rendered and a message may be present in the working message area (WS-MESSAGE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen message area is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the content of the working message area (WS-MESSAGE) — which may contain a validation error message, a success confirmation, or spaces if no message is pending — into the screen's error/message display field (ERRMSGO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Pending Message in Screen Message Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: Any pending informational or error message that was set prior to displaying the Add User screen must be transferred to the visible screen message area so the user can see it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All screen header fields, message area, and data entry fields have been populated in the output map (COUSR1AO)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen to the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system renders the Add User form (map COUSR1A from mapset COUSR01) to the terminal, erasing any previously displayed content, and positions the cursor at the field designated by the cursor-positioning indicator, leaving the screen awaiting user input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Render Add User Data Entry Form to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all header and message fields have been populated, the fully assembled Add User data entry form must be sent to the user's terminal, clearing any previous screen content and positioning the cursor as directed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has previously been presented with the Add User screen and has entered data into one or more of the following fields: First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the Add User screen by pressing any key (Enter, PF3, PF4, or any other key)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures and retains all data entered by the user across all five fields — First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type — from the Add User screen into the input data area, making the submitted values available for subsequent key press handling and field-level validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture User Input from Add User Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user submits the Add User screen, the system must capture all data entered across the five input fields — First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type — before proceeding to validate the submitted data or handle the key press action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add User screen has been displayed to the user and the user has interacted with the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the following five fields from the screen submission: (1) First Name, (2) Last Name, (3) User ID, (4) Password, and (5) User Type — all of which are subsequently available for mandatory field validation and new user record creation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fields Available for Processing After Screen Submission
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Add User screen collects exactly five user-provided data fields. All five fields must be captured upon screen submission so they are available for mandatory field validation and subsequent user record creation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is in an active session and has already been presented with the Add User screen at least once (the session is in re-entry state)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the Add User screen by pressing any key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system first completes capturing all user-entered field data from the screen, and only after successful capture does it proceed to evaluate the key pressed (Enter, PF3, PF4, or other) to determine the next action — ensuring no key press handling occurs before all submitted field values are available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Input Capture Precedes Key Press Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must complete the capture of all user-entered screen data before evaluating which key the user pressed and determining the appropriate action to take. Screen data capture is a mandatory prerequisite step to key press handling.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User Add screen with an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Admin Menu screen (COADM01C) and initiates the return-to-previous-screen navigation process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Admin Menu as Navigation Destination on PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the User Add screen, the system designates the Admin Menu screen (COADM01C) as the target navigation destination before initiating the return navigation flow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The navigation process has been initiated and the destination program field is either empty or contains no value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the destination program before navigating
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system overrides the missing destination and sets it to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) as the default navigation target

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Navigation Destination to Sign-On Screen When Destination is Missing
all_rules.Rule_Description: As a safety fallback during navigation, if the destination program has not been set or is blank, the system defaults the navigation target to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined the navigation destination (either Admin Menu COADM01C or defaulted to Sign-On COSGN00C)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the destination screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current Transaction ID into the 'From Transaction ID' field of the communication area, records the current Program Name into the 'From Program' field of the communication area, and resets the Program Context indicator to zero

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Current Session Context Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before navigating away from the User Add screen, the system records the current session's Transaction ID and Program Name into the shared communication area, and resets the program context indicator to zero, so the destination screen has full knowledge of where the navigation originated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program has been set (Admin Menu COADM01C or defaulted to Sign-On COSGN00C) and the current session details (Transaction ID, Program Name, Program Context) have been recorded in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers full control to the destination screen and passes the complete session communication area (containing Transaction ID, Program Name, and Program Context) to the destination screen, so no further processing occurs on the User Add screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Destination Screen with Session Context
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system transfers full control to the destination screen (Admin Menu COADM01C or Sign-On COSGN00C as fallback), passing along the complete session communication area so the destination screen has access to all relevant session information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen and has pressed a function key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed is PF4
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system initiates the Clear Current Screen process, which clears all input fields and redisplays a blank Add User form

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect PF4 Key Press and Trigger Clear Screen Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the PF4 key on the Add User screen, the system recognizes this as a request to clear all entered data and restart data entry from a blank form.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name input field (FNAMEI) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously entered value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear First Name Input Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, the First Name input field on the Add User screen is reset to blank/empty.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Last Name input field (LNAMEI) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously entered value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Last Name Input Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, the Last Name input field on the Add User screen is reset to blank/empty.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID input field (USERIDI) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously entered value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear User ID Input Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, the User ID input field on the Add User screen is reset to blank/empty.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Password input field (PASSWDI) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously entered value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Password Input Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, the Password input field on the Add User screen is reset to blank/empty.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Type input field (USRTYPEI) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously entered value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear User Type Input Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, the User Type input field on the Add User screen is reset to blank/empty.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 on the Add User screen and the clear screen process has been initiated, and there may be an existing error or status message displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message area (WS-MESSAGE and ERRMSGO) is cleared to spaces, removing any previously displayed error or status message from the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Existing Error or Status Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the PF4 clear screen operation, any existing error or status message currently displayed on the Add User screen is removed so the user sees a clean form without any prior messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF4 and all input fields and messages have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the blank Add User form
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor is set to the First Name field (FNAMEL length indicator set to -1) so that focus is placed on First Name when the screen is rendered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Cursor Focus to First Name Field After Clear
all_rules.Rule_Description: After clearing all fields during the PF4 operation, the system positions the cursor on the First Name field so the user can immediately begin fresh data entry without manually navigating to the first field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to display the blank Add User form following a PF4 clear operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population routine is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID), the current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME), the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY), and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Current Date, Time, and Program Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the blank Add User form after a PF4 clear, the system refreshes the screen header with the current date, current time, application titles, transaction ID, and program name to ensure the header information is always up to date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All input fields have been cleared to spaces, the message area is empty, the cursor is set to the First Name field, and the screen header has been populated with current date, time, transaction ID, and program name
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen (Map COUSR1A from Mapset COUSR01) to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is fully erased and redrawn showing a blank Add User form with no data in any input field, no error or status message displayed, the cursor positioned on the First Name field, and the header showing current date, time, transaction ID, and program name — allowing the user to begin fresh data entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Blank Add User Form with Cleared Fields and No Messages
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all fields are cleared and the header is populated, the system sends the blank Add User form to the user's screen, erasing any previous screen content and positioning the cursor on the First Name field, enabling the user to begin fresh data entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen and has previously entered or not entered any data in the user fields (First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, User Type)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key that is NOT the Enter key, NOT PF3, and NOT PF4
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies the key press as invalid and initiates the invalid key error handling process, without processing any entered data or performing any save operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Invalid Key Press on Add User Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses any key other than Enter, PF3, or PF4 on the Add User screen, the system identifies it as an invalid key action and triggers the error handling flow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed a key on the Add User screen that is not Enter, PF3, or PF4
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the key press is invalid (falls into the 'any other key' category)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error indicator flag to 'Y' (active/on), marking the current interaction as an error state so the screen is redisplayed in error mode

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Error Indicator on Invalid Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an invalid key is detected, the system activates the error indicator flag to signal that an error condition exists, which will control subsequent screen display behavior.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error indicator has been set due to an invalid key press on the Add User screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the invalid key error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system loads the standard application-defined invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE), which will be displayed to the user in the error message area of the Add User screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load Invalid Key Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an invalid key press is detected, the system loads the standard invalid key error message into the screen message area to inform the user of the incorrect action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected an invalid key press and loaded the invalid key error message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Add User screen with the error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the cursor position indicator for the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI) to -1, which instructs the screen to place the cursor on the First Name input field when the screen is rendered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Cursor Focus to First Name Field on Invalid Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: After an invalid key press, the system directs the cursor to the First Name input field so the user's attention is guided to the beginning of the form for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error indicator is set to active, the invalid key error message is loaded into WS-MESSAGE, and the cursor is directed to the First Name field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with current date (MM/DD/YY format), current time (HH:MM:SS format), transaction ID, and program name; moves the error message from WS-MESSAGE into the screen error message display field (ERRMSGO of COUSR1AO); and redisplays the full Add User screen (MAP COUSR1A, MAPSET COUSR01) with the cursor positioned on the First Name field and all previously entered field values retained on screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Add User Screen with Invalid Key Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system redisplays the Add User screen with the invalid key error message visible, the cursor on the First Name field, and all previously entered data preserved, so the user can review the error and take the correct action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add User screen is displayed and the user has pressed the Enter key to submit the form
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The First Name field contains only blank spaces or is completely empty (low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) activate the error flag to indicate a validation failure, (2) set the error message to 'First Name can NOT be empty...', (3) position the cursor focus on the First Name field, and (4) redisplay the Add User screen showing the error message — no further field validations are performed and the user record is NOT saved

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Name Mandatory Field Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user submits the Add User form by pressing the Enter key, the system must verify that the First Name field contains a value. If the First Name field is blank or empty, the submission is rejected and the user is prompted to provide a First Name.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key to submit the Add User form
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The First Name field is blank or empty (spaces or low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to ON ('Y'), which prevents any further processing such as saving the new user record to the system

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Flag Activation on First Name Validation Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the First Name field is found to be blank or empty upon form submission, the system activates an internal error flag to signal that a validation error has occurred, preventing the user record from being saved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error flag has been activated due to the First Name field being blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Add User screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message displayed on the screen must be exactly: 'First Name can NOT be empty...'

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Name Empty Error Message Assignment
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the First Name field fails the mandatory field check, the system assigns a specific, user-friendly error message to inform the user exactly which field requires attention and what the issue is.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The First Name field has been found to be blank or empty upon form submission
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Add User screen is being prepared for redisplay with the error message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor focus must be set to the First Name input field so that the user can immediately begin correcting the value without manually navigating to the field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Positioning to First Name Field on Validation Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the First Name field fails validation, the system automatically positions the screen cursor on the First Name input field to guide the user directly to the field that requires correction, improving the user experience.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The First Name field is blank or empty, the error flag is ON, the error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...' has been set, and the cursor is positioned on the First Name field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Add User screen (COUSR1A) is redisplayed with: (1) the error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...' visible on screen, (2) the cursor positioned on the First Name field, (3) all previously entered data for other fields retained on screen, and (4) the screen header updated with current date and time

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Add User Screen with First Name Validation Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After detecting that the First Name field is empty and setting the appropriate error message and cursor position, the system redisplays the Add User screen so the user can see the error and make the necessary correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key to submit the Add User form
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The First Name field contains a non-blank, non-empty value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does not raise any error for the First Name field and proceeds immediately to validate the Last Name field as the next step in the sequential validation process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Last Name Validation When First Name is Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the First Name field contains a valid non-empty value, the system proceeds to the next sequential validation step — checking the Last Name field — as part of the mandatory field validation sequence for the Add User form.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen and has pressed the ENTER key to submit the form, and the First Name field has already been validated successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Last Name field is blank or contains no value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error indicator to active, (2) set the error message to 'Last Name can NOT be empty...', (3) set the cursor focus to the Last Name input field, and (4) redisplay the Add User screen with the error message visible, halting further validation until the user corrects the Last Name field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Last Name Mandatory Field Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Last Name field is not blank or empty when a user submits the Add User form. This rule ensures that every new user record must have a Last Name value before it can be saved to the system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen and has pressed the ENTER key to submit the form, and the First Name field has already been validated successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Last Name field contains a non-blank, non-empty value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does not set any error flag or error message for the Last Name field, and immediately proceeds to validate the User ID field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Last Name Valid – Proceed to User ID Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Last Name field contains a valid non-blank value, the system proceeds to the next sequential validation step, which is the User ID field check. No action or message is triggered for the Last Name field itself.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Last Name field has been found to be blank or empty during form submission validation, and the error flag has been set with the message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' and cursor positioned on the Last Name field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is instructed to send the Add User screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) populate the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction ID, and program name, (2) place the error message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' in the screen error message area, and (3) redisplay the Add User screen with all previously entered field values retained and the cursor positioned on the Last Name field, awaiting user correction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Add User Screen with Last Name Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Last Name validation fails, the system refreshes and redisplays the Add User screen, showing the error message to the user. The screen header is also refreshed with the current date, time, transaction ID, and program name before display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Add User form by pressing the ENTER key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The First Name field is blank or empty OR the Last Name field is blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system stops validation at the failed field (First Name or Last Name), displays the corresponding error message, and does NOT proceed to validate the User ID field

all_rules.Rule_Name: User ID Validation Prerequisite - Sequential Validation Order
all_rules.Rule_Description: User ID validation is only reached if First Name and Last Name have both already passed their respective validations. The system enforces a strict sequential order of field validation, stopping at the first failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Add User form by pressing the ENTER key, and both First Name and Last Name fields have passed their validations
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field contains only spaces or low-values (is blank or empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to ON, sets the error message to 'User ID can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor focus on the User ID field, and redisplays the Add User screen with the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: User ID Mandatory Field Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits the Add User form, the User ID field must not be blank or empty. This validation only executes after First Name and Last Name have successfully passed their validations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Add User form and both First Name and Last Name have passed validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field is blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y' (ON), which blocks any attempt to write the new user record to the security file

all_rules.Rule_Name: User ID Error Flag Activation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID field is found to be blank or empty upon form submission, the system activates the error flag to indicate a validation failure, which prevents the user record from being saved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Add User form and the User ID field has been determined to be blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID validation fails due to blank or empty value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen error message to exactly 'User ID can NOT be empty...'

all_rules.Rule_Name: User ID Empty Error Message Assignment
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID field is blank or empty, the system assigns a specific business error message to inform the user that the User ID is a required field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User ID field has been determined to be blank or empty upon form submission
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Add User screen with the validation error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the cursor focus position to the User ID input field so that the user can immediately begin entering the User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: User ID Field Cursor Focus on Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID field fails validation, the system directs the user's attention by positioning the cursor directly on the User ID field, enabling immediate correction without manual navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User ID field is blank or empty, the error flag is set to ON, the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' has been assigned, and the cursor is set to the User ID field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Add User screen (COUSR1A) is displayed with the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' visible, the cursor positioned on the User ID field, and all previously entered data in other fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) retained on screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Add User Screen Redisplay with User ID Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a User ID validation failure, the system redisplays the Add User screen populated with the error message and cursor positioned on the User ID field, allowing the user to correct the missing value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Add User form, and First Name, Last Name, and User ID fields have all passed their respective validations
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field contains a non-blank and non-empty value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does not set any error flag or error message for User ID, and proceeds to evaluate whether the Password field is blank or empty

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Password Validation When User ID is Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID field contains a non-blank, non-empty value, the system considers the User ID validation passed and advances to validate the Password field as the next step in the sequential validation chain.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen and has already provided valid values for First Name, Last Name, and User ID fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the ENTER key to submit the form and the Password field is blank or empty (contains only spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to ON, displays the error message 'Password can NOT be empty...' on the Add User screen, and the form submission is halted — no user record is saved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Password Field Must Not Be Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user submits the Add User form, the system must validate that the Password field contains a value. If the Password field is blank or empty, the system must reject the submission and notify the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Password field validation has failed because the Password field is blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Add User screen with the error message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor focus is set to the Password field so that the user can immediately enter the required password value without manually navigating to the field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Cursor Focus to Password Field on Validation Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Password field fails validation (is blank or empty), the system must direct the user's cursor to the Password field to facilitate immediate correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Password field validation has failed, the error flag is set to ON, the error message 'Password can NOT be empty...' is set, and the cursor is positioned on the Password field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Add User screen is displayed with: (1) the error message 'Password can NOT be empty...' visible to the user, (2) the cursor positioned on the Password field, (3) the screen header populated with current Transaction ID, Program Name, current Date (MM/DD/YY), and current Time (HH:MM:SS), and (4) all previously entered field values retained on screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Add User Screen with Password Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Password field is found to be empty upon form submission, the system must redisplay the Add User screen showing the specific password error message along with updated header information including current date and time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add User screen has been redisplayed with the error message 'Password can NOT be empty...' and the cursor is on the Password field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters a value in the Password field and presses the ENTER key to resubmit the form
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system receives the updated screen input and re-evaluates the Password field — if the Password field now contains a value, the system proceeds to validate the User Type field; if the Password field is still blank or empty, the same error message 'Password can NOT be empty...' is displayed again with the cursor repositioned on the Password field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-Validate Password After User Correction and Resubmission
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Password validation error is displayed, the user may correct the Password field and resubmit the form. The system must re-enter the full validation sequence starting from the Password validation step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen and has filled in First Name, Last Name, User ID, and Password fields with valid non-blank values, but has left the User Type field empty or blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the ENTER key to submit the Add User form
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the Error Flag to ON ('Y'), (2) Set the error message to 'User Type can NOT be empty...', (3) Set the cursor focus to the User Type input field, and (4) Redisplay the Add User screen showing the error message — and the new user record must NOT be saved to the system

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Type Field Mandatory Validation on Add User Form
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user submits the Add User form, the User Type field must contain a valid non-blank value. If the User Type field is left empty or blank, the system must prevent submission, activate the error state, display a specific error message, and redirect cursor focus to the User Type field so the user can correct the entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add User screen and all five fields (First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type) have been filled with valid non-blank values, and no validation error flag has been raised during the sequential field validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Type field passes the mandatory check (is not empty or blank) and the Error Flag remains OFF
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Map the entered User ID to the new user record's User ID, (2) Map the entered First Name to the new user record's First Name, (3) Map the entered Last Name to the new user record's Last Name, (4) Map the entered Password to the new user record's Password, (5) Map the entered User Type to the new user record's User Type, and (6) Invoke the Save New User process to write the complete user record to the security file

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Type Field Valid – Proceed to Save New User Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all five mandatory fields on the Add User form — First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type — contain valid non-blank values and no error flag has been raised during the sequential validation process, the system proceeds to prepare and save the new user record to the security file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Add User form by pressing the ENTER key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All mandatory field validations (First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type) have passed with no errors flagged
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to map all entered screen values into the user security record structure in preparation for saving; if any validation error exists, this entire preparation step is bypassed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger User Record Preparation Only When All Validations Pass
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must only proceed to prepare and populate the new user security record when all mandatory field validations have passed without any errors. If any validation has failed, the record preparation is skipped entirely.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All mandatory field validations have passed and the system is preparing the new user security record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system maps the screen input fields to the user security record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID value entered on the Add User screen is assigned to the User ID field of the user security record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Entered User ID from Screen to User Security Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all validations pass, the User ID value entered by the operator on the Add User screen is transferred into the User ID field of the user security record, making it ready for storage.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All mandatory field validations have passed and the User ID has been mapped to the user security record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues mapping the remaining screen input fields to the user security record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name value entered on the Add User screen is assigned to the First Name field of the user security record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Entered First Name from Screen to User Security Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all validations pass, the First Name value entered by the operator on the Add User screen is transferred into the First Name field of the user security record, making it ready for storage.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All mandatory field validations have passed and the First Name has been mapped to the user security record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues mapping the remaining screen input fields to the user security record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Last Name value entered on the Add User screen is assigned to the Last Name field of the user security record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Entered Last Name from Screen to User Security Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all validations pass, the Last Name value entered by the operator on the Add User screen is transferred into the Last Name field of the user security record, making it ready for storage.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All mandatory field validations have passed and the Last Name has been mapped to the user security record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues mapping the remaining screen input fields to the user security record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Password value entered on the Add User screen is assigned to the Password field of the user security record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Entered Password from Screen to User Security Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all validations pass, the Password value entered by the operator on the Add User screen is transferred into the Password field of the user security record, making it ready for storage.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All mandatory field validations have passed and the Password has been mapped to the user security record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system maps the final screen input field to the user security record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Type value entered on the Add User screen is assigned to the User Type field of the user security record, and the complete user security record — containing User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type — is fully prepared and ready to be saved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Entered User Type from Screen to User Security Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all validations pass, the User Type value entered by the operator on the Add User screen is transferred into the User Type field of the user security record, completing the record preparation and making it fully ready for saving.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All mandatory field validations have passed with no errors and the system is preparing the new user security record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field mapping process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The five fields are mapped in the following strict sequence: (1) User ID, (2) First Name, (3) Last Name, (4) Password, (5) User Type — and only after all five fields are mapped is the user security record considered complete and ready to be saved to the system

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Security Record Field Mapping Sequence
all_rules.Rule_Description: The preparation of the new user security record follows a strict sequential order: User ID is mapped first, followed by First Name, Last Name, Password, and finally User Type. All five fields must be mapped before the record is considered complete and ready for saving.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All five mandatory fields (First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type) have been entered and passed validation with no errors flagged
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to save the new user record to the User Security File (USRSEC) using the User ID as the unique record key, storing First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type along with it
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new user record containing User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type is written to the User Security File (USRSEC), and the system evaluates whether the save was successful, resulted in a duplicate User ID, or encountered an unexpected failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save New User Record to User Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all mandatory user fields have been validated successfully, the system saves the new user's details to the User Security File (USRSEC) using the User ID as the unique identifier for the record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to save a new user record to the User Security File (USRSEC)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The save operation completes successfully (normal response received from the User Security File)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears all input fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) and the message area, displays a green-colored confirmation message in the format 'User [User ID] has been added ...' where [User ID] is the newly added User ID, and presents a blank User Add form with the cursor positioned on the First Name field, ready for the next user entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Success Confirmation After New User is Added
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new user record is successfully saved to the User Security File, the system confirms the addition with a green-colored success message that includes the newly added User ID, clears all input fields, and presents a blank form ready for the next user entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to save a new user record to the User Security File (USRSEC) with a specific User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The save operation fails because the User ID already exists in the User Security File (duplicate key or duplicate record response is received)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'User ID already exist...' on the screen, and repositions the cursor focus to the User ID input field so the user can enter a different, unique User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Duplicate User ID During User Creation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new user record cannot be saved because the entered User ID already exists in the User Security File, the system rejects the addition and notifies the user that the User ID is already in use, directing them to correct it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to save a new user record to the User Security File (USRSEC)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The save operation fails for any reason other than a duplicate User ID (an unexpected or unrecognized failure response is received)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'Unable to Add User...' on the screen, and repositions the cursor focus to the First Name input field so the user can review and resubmit the form

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Unexpected Failure When Adding New User
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new user record cannot be saved due to an unexpected system failure (not a duplicate User ID), the system notifies the user that the addition was unsuccessful and allows them to retry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new user record has been successfully saved to the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the successful save confirmation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All input fields on the Add User form are cleared to blank: User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type are all set to empty spaces, and the cursor is positioned on the First Name field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Input Fields After Successful User Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a new user record is successfully saved to the security file, all input fields on the Add User form must be reset to blank so the screen is ready for the next user entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new user record has been successfully saved to the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to display the success confirmation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message area on the Add User screen is cleared of any previously displayed error or informational messages before the new success message is rendered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Existing Error or Status Messages After Successful Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: Any previously displayed error or status messages on the Add User screen must be cleared before the success confirmation message is shown, ensuring no stale messages remain visible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new user record has been successfully saved to the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the success confirmation message for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message display color attribute on the Add User screen is set to green, so the success message is rendered in green text

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Success Message in Green Color
all_rules.Rule_Description: To visually distinguish a successful user addition from error conditions, the success confirmation message must be displayed in green color on the Add User screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new user record has been successfully saved to the User Security File with a specific User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the confirmation message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The success message is constructed in the format: 'User [UserID] has been added ...' where [UserID] is the actual User ID that was just saved, with leading/trailing spaces in the User ID trimmed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build User Addition Success Message with User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful creation of a new user, the system must construct a confirmation message that includes the newly added User ID, providing clear feedback to the operator about which user was created.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to display the Add User screen following a successful user save
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header is populated before display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header is updated with: (1) Application Title Line 1 and Title Line 2 from the application constants, (2) the current Transaction ID, (3) the current Program Name, (4) the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, and (5) the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS — all reflecting real-time values at the moment of display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Add User Screen Header with Current Session and Date/Time Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the Add User screen is rendered — including after a successful save — the screen header must be refreshed with the current application titles, program name, transaction ID, and the real-time current date and time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All input fields have been cleared, the success message has been built in green, and the screen header has been populated with current session and date/time information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Add User screen to the operator's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Add User screen (COUSR1A from map set COUSR01) is displayed with: (1) all input fields blank and ready for new input, (2) the green-colored success message 'User [UserID] has been added ...' visible in the message area, (3) the updated header showing current application title, program name, transaction ID, date, and time, and (4) the cursor positioned on the First Name field — the screen is fully ready for the next user addition

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Blank Add User Form with Green Success Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully adding a user, the system must present a fully cleared Add User form alongside the green success message, enabling the operator to immediately begin entering the next new user without any additional navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has filled in all required fields on the Add User screen and submitted the form, and the system has attempted to write the new user record to the security file using the entered User ID as the unique record key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The security file write operation returns a Duplicate Key response or a Duplicate Record response, indicating that the entered User ID already exists in the security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must recognize this as a duplicate User ID condition and initiate the duplicate user ID error handling process, preventing the new user record from being saved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Duplicate User ID on Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new user record is being saved, the system must check whether the entered User ID already exists in the security file. If a duplicate key or duplicate record condition is detected, the system must prevent the save and trigger the duplicate user ID error handling flow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to save a new user record to the security file and the write operation has returned a Duplicate Key or Duplicate Record response
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The duplicate User ID condition is confirmed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the session error flag to 'Y' (error active), marking the current session as being in an error state and preventing any successful completion processing from occurring

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Session as Error State for Duplicate User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a duplicate User ID is detected during the save operation, the system must flag the current session as being in an error state so that subsequent processing is aware that the add user operation did not complete successfully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The session error flag has been set to active due to a duplicate User ID being detected during the save operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the error response to display to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the screen error message to exactly 'User ID already exist...' so the user understands that the specific User ID they entered is already registered in the system

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Duplicate User ID Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a duplicate User ID is detected, the system must communicate the specific reason for the failure to the user by setting a clear, descriptive error message indicating that the entered User ID is already in use.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected a duplicate User ID condition and has set the error message to 'User ID already exist...'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Add User screen with the error information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the cursor position indicator for the User ID field to -1, which directs the screen cursor to be placed on the User ID input field when the screen is redisplayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Cursor Focus to User ID Field on Duplicate Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a duplicate User ID error is detected, the system must guide the user directly to the field that requires correction by positioning the screen cursor on the User ID input field, enabling the user to immediately enter a different User ID without manually navigating to that field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The session error flag is set to active, the error message is set to 'User ID already exist...', and the cursor focus is directed to the User ID field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the Send Add User Screen process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must populate the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY format), current time (HH:MM:SS format), transaction ID, and program name, then display the Add User screen with the error message 'User ID already exist...' visible and the cursor positioned on the User ID field, allowing the user to enter a different User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Add User Screen with Duplicate User ID Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After setting the duplicate User ID error state, error message, and cursor position, the system must redisplay the Add User screen so the user can see the error message and correct the User ID. The screen redisplay includes refreshing the header information with current date and time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new user record has been submitted for saving to the User Security File with all mandatory fields (First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, User Type) populated and the User ID is not a duplicate
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The save operation to the User Security File completes with an outcome that is not a successful write and not a duplicate User ID or duplicate record condition — i.e., an unexpected system or data error occurs
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must identify the result as an unexpected save failure and proceed to activate the error handling sequence, which includes setting the error flag, displaying an error message, and returning the Add User screen to the user for retry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Unexpected User Save Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system attempts to save a new user record to the security file and the result is neither a successful write nor a duplicate key/record condition, the system identifies this as an unexpected save failure and triggers the error handling path.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to save a new user record to the User Security File and the save result is an unexpected error (not success, not duplicate)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The unexpected error condition is detected from the save operation result
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the Error Flag to ON (value 'Y' in WS-ERR-FLG) to mark the transaction as failed and block any downstream processing of the user record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Activate Error State on Unexpected Save Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs during the save of a new user record, the system must activate the error flag to indicate that the current transaction is in an error state, preventing any further processing of the user record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to save a new user record to the User Security File and the save result is an unexpected error (not success, not duplicate)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error flag has been set to ON due to the unexpected save failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the screen error message to exactly 'Unable to Add User...' (stored in WS-MESSAGE) so that this message will be presented to the user on the Add User screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display 'Unable to Add User' Error Message on Unexpected Save Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while saving a new user record, the system must set a specific business error message to inform the user that the add operation could not be completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has encountered an unexpected error while saving a new user record to the User Security File and the error message 'Unable to Add User...' has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Add User screen following the unexpected save failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the cursor position to the First Name field (FNAMEL of COUSR1AI set to -1) so that when the Add User screen is redisplayed, the cursor is automatically placed on the First Name input field for the user to begin reviewing their input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reposition Cursor to First Name Field After Save Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while saving a new user record, the system must direct the user's cursor focus back to the First Name field on the Add User screen, guiding the user to review and re-enter data from the beginning of the form.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has set the error flag to ON, the error message to 'Unable to Add User...', and the cursor focus to the First Name field following an unexpected save failure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the Send Add User Screen function (SEND-USRADD-SCREEN), which populates the screen header with the current Transaction ID, Program Name, current Date (MM/DD/YY), and current Time (HH:MM:SS) before sending the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Add User screen (COUSR1A from mapset COUSR01) must be redisplayed to the user with: (1) the error message 'Unable to Add User...' shown in the message area, (2) the cursor positioned on the First Name field, (3) all previously entered field values retained on screen, and (4) the screen header showing current date, time, transaction ID, and program name — enabling the user to review the error and retry adding the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Add User Screen with Save Failure Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After an unexpected error occurs during the save of a new user record, the system must redisplay the Add User screen with the error message and updated header information, allowing the user to review the error and retry the operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Add screen is accessed and no prior session context exists (communication area length is zero, indicating no active session has been established)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the absence of a prior session context at program entry
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and initiates navigation to that screen, preventing access to the User Add functionality without a valid session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redirect to Sign-On Screen When No Prior Session Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User Add screen is invoked without any prior session context, the system must immediately redirect the user to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to establish a valid session before proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to navigate the user away from the User Add screen and the destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is either blank (spaces) or contains no value (low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return-to-previous-screen process is triggered and the destination program is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system overrides the blank or unset destination and sets it to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) as the default navigation target, ensuring no navigation occurs to an undefined screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Destination to Sign-On Screen When Destination Program Is Not Set
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before navigating away from the User Add screen, the system must verify that a destination program has been explicitly set. If the destination is blank or not set, the system defaults the navigation target to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined the destination program and is preparing to navigate the user away from the User Add screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The navigation process records session origin details prior to transferring control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures and stores the current transaction identifier (WS-TRANID) as the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the session communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Transaction and Program in Session Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before navigating the user to another screen, the system must record the current transaction identifier and the current program name into the session context. This preserves the originating transaction and program information so the destination screen knows where the navigation originated from.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has recorded the originating transaction and program in the session and is about to transfer control to the destination screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session context is cleared as the final step before navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the session program context indicator (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) to zero, signaling to the destination screen that this is a new entry and not a re-entry from a previous interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Session Program Context Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Immediately before transferring control to the destination screen, the system must reset the session program context to zero. This ensures that the destination screen treats the incoming navigation as a fresh entry rather than a re-entry, preventing stale context from affecting the destination screen's behavior.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program has been set (either explicitly to COSGN00C or defaulted to COSGN00C), the originating transaction and program have been recorded, and the session program context has been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) passing the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) containing the originating transaction identifier, originating program name, and cleared program context, so the Sign-On screen can process the incoming navigation correctly

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate User to Sign-On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all session context has been recorded and cleared, the system transfers control to the resolved destination screen (Sign-On screen COSGN00C), passing the updated session communication area so the destination screen has full context of the navigation origin.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user interaction has completed (any key press has been processed — ENTER, PF3, PF4, or any other key) and the system is about to return control back to the transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to end the current processing cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must retain the current CARDDEMO-COMMAREA (containing session data including CDEMO-FROM-TRANID set to WS-TRANID, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM set to WS-PGMNAME, CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT, and CDEMO-PGM-REENTER flag) and pass it forward with the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) so that the next interaction resumes with full session continuity

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Session Communication Area Before Returning Control
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the end of every user interaction cycle, the system must retain all current session information — including the Transaction ID, Program Name, and the full Communication Area — so that the session context is not lost between interactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All processing for the current user interaction has been completed, including any screen sends, validations, data writes, or navigation decisions
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the final return step at the end of MAIN-PARA
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system returns control using the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) and passes the full CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, so that the transaction remains active, the session state is preserved, and the system is ready to receive the next user interaction without loss of context

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to Current Transaction with Session Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: After every user interaction is fully processed — whether it results in a screen display, a navigation action, or a data save — the system must explicitly return control to the same transaction using the preserved Communication Area, ensuring the session remains active and ready for the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has triggered a navigation action (PF3 pressed to go to Admin Menu COADM01C, or no active session detected redirecting to Sign-On COSGN00C)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN procedure
