Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) verify the destination program is set — if CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM is empty or low-values, default it to COSGN00C; (2) set CDEMO-FROM-TRANID to WS-TRANID (current transaction); (3) set CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM to WS-PGMNAME (current program name); (4) set CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT to zeros; and (5) transfer control to the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) passing the updated CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, so the destination screen has full context of the originating session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session Continuity Across Navigation to Previous Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user navigates away from the User Add screen (e.g., via PF3 to Admin Menu or when no session exists and redirected to Sign-On), the system must stamp the Communication Area with the originating Transaction ID and Program Name before transferring control, ensuring the destination screen knows where the user came from.

description:
COUSR01C is a CICS online program within the CardDemo application that handles the addition of new Regular or Admin users to the USRSEC security file. The program presents a user addition screen, validates all required fields (First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type), and writes the new user record to the USRSEC CICS file, providing appropriate success or error messages. Based on the use of EIBCALEN and EXEC CICS XCTL/RETURN with COMMAREA, this is a Main/Driver program that can transfer control to other screens.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS File - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Initialize Add User Session - When the program is first entered (no prior session), initialize the Add User screen with empty fields and set cursor focus to the First Name field, then display the screen to the user. 2: Display Add User Screen - Populate the screen header with application title, program name, transaction ID, current date, and current time, then render the Add User data entry form to the user. 3: Receive User Input - Capture all data entered by the user on the Add User screen, including First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type fields. 4: Handle PF3 Key - Navigate back to the Admin Menu screen (COADM01C) when the user presses PF3, passing the current session context. 5: Handle PF4 Key - Clear all input fields on the Add User screen and redisplay a blank form, allowing the user to start data entry over. 6: Handle Invalid Key Press - Display an invalid key error message to the user when any key other than Enter, PF3, or PF4 is pressed, and return focus to the First Name field. 7: Validate First Name - Check that the First Name field is not blank or empty. If empty, display the error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...' and set cursor focus to the First Name field. 8: Validate Last Name - Check that the Last Name field is not blank or empty. If empty, display the error message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' and set cursor focus to the Last Name field. 9: Validate User ID - Check that the User ID field is not blank or empty. If empty, display the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' and set cursor focus to the User ID field. 10: Validate Password - Check that the Password field is not blank or empty. If empty, display the error message 'Password can NOT be empty...' and set cursor focus to the Password field. 11: Validate User Type - Check that the User Type field is not blank or empty. If empty, display the error message 'User Type can NOT be empty...' and set cursor focus to the User Type field. 12: Prepare New User Record - After all validations pass, map the entered screen values (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) into the user security record structure in preparation for saving. 13: Save New User to Security File - Write the new user record to the User Security file (USRSEC) using the User ID as the unique record key. 14: Confirm Successful User Addition - Upon successful save, clear all input fields, display a green success message confirming the new user (e.g., 'User [UserID] has been added...'), and present a blank form ready for another entry. 15: Handle Duplicate User ID - If the User ID already exists in the security file, display the error message 'User ID already exist...' and set cursor focus to the User ID field so the user can enter a different ID. 16: Handle User Save Failure - If the user record cannot be saved due to an unexpected error, display the error message 'Unable to Add User...' and set cursor focus to the First Name field. 17: Return to Sign-On Screen - If no prior session context exists or the destination program is not set, navigate the user back to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C). 18: Maintain Session Context - At the end of each interaction, return control to the transaction with the current session communication area preserved, ensuring continuity of the user session.
